Name: Event Studio
Author: xzqute
Description:
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/Aa4rG0O.png[/img][/center]
[center][url=https://smapi.io][img]https://img.shields.io/badge/SMAPI-4.5.0+-brightgreen.svg[/img][/url]  [img]https://img.shields.io/badge/Stardew%20Valley-1.6.15-orange.svg[/img]  [img]https://img.shields.io/badge/Status-BETA-yellow.svg[/img]  [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/1915][img]https://img.shields.io/badge/Export-Content%20Patcher%202.9+-purple.svg[/img][/url][/center]
[center][size=4]Build Stardew Valley events inside the game, preview them on the actual map, and export the result as a Content Patcher pack.[/size][/center]

[heading][size=5]What it does[/size][/heading]
[size=4]Stardew Valley Event Studio is an in-game editor for building and editing Stardew Valley events without having to write the full event string by hand.[/size]

[size=4]Everything is built on the actual game location. You can add actors, place them on tiles, set up movement and dialogue, create questions and branches, control the camera, add animations and effects, and play the scene back without leaving the editor.[/size]

[size=4]Underneath the editor, the project still uses Stardew Valley's normal event format. Event Studio gives the vanilla commands a visual editing layer, then exports them back as normal Content Patcher event data.[/size]

[size=4]Right now, Event Studio includes:[/size]
[list]
[*][size=4]39 Actions available directly from the Action palette.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Dedicated editors for movement, animation, dialogue, questions, camera work, props, audio, rewards and other event commands.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]A multi-track timeline with playback, scrubbing, action stepping, grouping and reordering.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Canvas Preview for fast editing and a separate in-game preview using Stardew Valley's actual Event runtime.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Import of events already loaded by the game, including Content Patcher changes.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Question, Quick Question and Fork editing.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Undo and Redo, autosaves, recovery files and project backups.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Export to a ready-to-test Content Patcher content pack.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4][img]https://i.imgur.com/7ZaHEwf.png[/img][/size]

[heading][size=5]Beta release[/size][/heading]
[size=4]I'm releasing Event Studio as a beta because I want to see how it holds up when other people use it for real events. It can already build complete scenes and import, preview, save and export projects, but some parts of the workflow are still rough and need testing outside my own projects.[/size]

[size=4]Bug reports are welcome, but usability feedback matters just as much. If something takes too many clicks, an editor is confusing, a control behaves differently from what you expected, or you tried to build something and couldn't figure out how, please report it.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Installation[/size][/heading]
[list]
[*][size=4]Install [url=https://smapi.io]SMAPI[/url] 4.5.0 or newer.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Download Stardew Valley Event Studio and extract its folder into [i]Stardew Valley/Mods[/i].[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Launch the game through SMAPI and load a save.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Press [b]F10[/b] to open Event Studio. You can also use [i]eventstudio[/i] in the SMAPI console.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[size=4]This build targets Stardew Valley 1.6.15 and is intended for single-player use.[/size]

[size=4]You do not need Content Patcher to open the editor. It is only required to run a pack exported by Event Studio. Generated packs target Content Patcher 2.9.0 or newer.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Working in Event Studio[/size][/heading]
[size=4]The game location you are standing in becomes the editing stage. You can move the editor camera independently, inspect tile and world coordinates, show a tile grid and enable collision visualization while building the scene.[/size]

[size=4]Actors are placed directly on the map. Hold [b]Shift[/b] while selecting actors to create a multi-selection. Moving that group keeps the formation between actors and creates simultaneous movement for them.[/size]

[size=4]You can also preview the scene in a different season, weather type or time of day. These changes are temporary, and Event Studio restores the original environment when the editing session ends.[/size]

[size=4]Available options include Spring, Summer, Fall and Winter, plus clear weather, rain, storm, snow, wind and green rain where the location supports them.[/size]

[heading][size=4]Timeline[/size][/heading]
[size=4]The timeline represents Stardew Valley's ordered event sequence. Clip positions and lengths are calculated from the action order and the known duration of each command.[/size]

[size=4]Because the result is still a vanilla event, commands cannot all be placed at arbitrary timestamps like clips in a video editor. The timeline makes the order and timing easier to see and edit.[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]Mouse wheel: scroll tracks.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Shift + wheel[/b]: horizontal scroll.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Ctrl + wheel[/b]: zoom the timeline around the mouse pointer.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Up / Down[/b]: select the previous or next action.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Enter[/b]: edit the selected action.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Space[/b]: enable or disable the selected action.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V / Ctrl+D[/b]: copy, paste or duplicate.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Ctrl+Up / Ctrl+Down[/b]: reorder actions.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]G[/b]: group or ungroup compatible adjacent actions into a simultaneous turn.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]W[/b]: wait for all movement in the selected simultaneous group.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]A[/b]: toggle asynchronous movement where the command supports it.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]P[/b]: Play / Pause Canvas Preview.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Home / End[/b]: jump to the start or end of the sequence.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Left / Right[/b]: step through actions.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[heading][size=4]Action editors[/size][/heading]
[size=4]Commands that need more than a few fields get their own visual editor instead of a generic property window.[/size]

[size=4]Movement actions can show the map, destination and generated route. Animation has a frame editor with playback and per-frame holds, while emotes use a visual picker. Audio can be previewed directly from its editor, and questions have a separate workflow for answers and branches. Item, quest, mail, actor and location fields can use searchable resource browsers, but you can still enter exact IDs manually.[/size]

[size=4]Nothing is written into the project until you press [b]Apply[/b]. Cancel or Escape throws away the draft. Each applied edit becomes a single history operation, so Undo restores the previous version of the action.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Supported Actions[/size][/heading]
[size=4]The Action palette contains [b]39 Actions[/b]. Some related vanilla commands share one editor, so the parser understands a few more command forms than the palette count suggests.[/size]

[heading][size=4]Dialogue and branching[/size][/heading]
[list]
[*][size=4][b]Dialogue[/b] ([i]speak[/i]): NPC or farmer dialogue with pages, portraits, expressions, placeholders, gender text and an optional i18n key.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Message[/b] ([i]message[/i]): show a message without a character portrait.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Text Above Head[/b] ([i]textAboveHead[/i]): display temporary text above an NPC.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Question[/b] ([i]question[/i] / [i]quickQuestion[/i]): create Event Result, Game Key and Quick Question choices.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Fork[/b] ([i]fork[/i]): branch into another action sequence using an answer, mail or condition ID, or special event result.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[heading][size=4]Movement[/size][/heading]
[list]
[*][size=4][b]Move[/b] ([i]move[/i]): move an actor to a tile with facing, speed override, async movement and Vanilla or Collision-aware routing.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Face Direction[/b] ([i]faceDirection[/i]): turn an actor to a selected direction.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Warp Actor[/b] ([i]warp[/i]): immediately move an actor to another tile.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Advanced Move[/b] ([i]advancedMove[/i]): build a route from ordered Walk and Face/Pause steps, with optional looping.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Stop Advanced Moves[/b] ([i]stopAdvancedMoves[/i]): stop advanced movement immediately or after its current step.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Position Offset[/b] ([i]positionOffset[/i]): apply a pixel offset without changing the actor's logical tile.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[heading][size=4]Actor animation and presentation[/size][/heading]
[list]
[*][size=4][b]Emote[/b] ([i]emote[/i]): choose a named emote or enter an emote ID.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Jump[/b] ([i]jump[/i]): configure jump velocity and optional sound suppression.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Shake Actor[/b] ([i]shake[/i]): shake an NPC for a selected duration.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Item Above Head[/b] ([i]itemAboveHead[/i]): make the farmer hold an item or supported special token overhead.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Show Frame[/b] ([i]showFrame[/i]): display a specific animation frame with optional horizontal flip.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Animate Actor[/b] ([i]animate[/i]): create a frame sequence with editable timing, looping and horizontal flip.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Stop Animation[/b] ([i]stopAnimation[/i]): stop the current actor animation and optionally choose the ending frame.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Sprite Offset[/b] ([i]drawOffset[/i]): change where an actor is drawn without moving its tile position.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Hide NPC Shadow[/b] ([i]hideShadow[/i]): hide or restore the shadow below an NPC.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[heading][size=4]Scene, camera and props[/size][/heading]
[list]
[*][size=4][b]Change Location[/b] ([i]changeLocation[/i]): continue the event on another game location.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Camera[/b] ([i]viewport[/i]): move the viewport to a selected area, with map clamping and optional fade behavior.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Camera Pan[/b] ([i]viewport move[/i]): move the camera over time using X/Y velocity and duration.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Fade[/b] ([i]fade[/i], [i]globalFade[/i], [i]globalFadeToClear[/i]): fade the screen to black or back to clear. Global fades also expose duration and continuation behavior.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Temporary Sprite[/b] ([i]temporarySprite[/i]): create a vanilla event sprite animation with row, frames, interval, flip and layer-depth settings.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Place Prop[/b] ([i]addObject[/i]): display an item as a temporary event prop on a tile.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Remove Prop[/b] ([i]removeObject[/i]): remove temporary event visuals from a tile.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[heading][size=4]Audio[/size][/heading]
[list]
[*][size=4][b]Play Sound[/b] ([i]playSound[/i]): select or enter a sound cue and preview it from the editor.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Play Music[/b] ([i]playMusic[/i]): change the event music. Preview sessions restore the previous soundtrack afterward.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[heading][size=4]Rewards and story progress[/size][/heading]
[list]
[*][size=4][b]Give Item[/b] ([i]addItem[/i]): give an item with count and quality.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Take Item[/b] ([i]removeItem[/i]): remove an item from the player's inventory.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Change Money[/b] ([i]money[/i]): add or subtract gold.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Change Friendship[/b] ([i]friendship[/i]): add or subtract friendship points for an NPC.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Add Quest[/b] ([i]addQuest[/i]): add a quest to the journal.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Remove Quest[/b] ([i]removeQuest[/i]): remove a quest from the journal.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Set Story Flag[/b] ([i]addMailReceived[/i]): set or clear a received-mail flag used by event conditions.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[heading][size=4]Event flow[/size][/heading]
[list]
[*][size=4][b]Pause[/b] ([i]pause[/i]): wait before running the next command.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Allow Skip[/b] ([i]skippable[/i]): allow the player to skip the event.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Disallow Skip[/b] ([i]unskippable[/i]): disable event skipping from that point.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[heading][size=5]Other commands understood by the editor[/size][/heading]
[size=4]The importer also understands several commands that do not have their own entry in the 39-item Action palette.[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]Imported [i]speed[/i] commands get a structured Actor Speed editor. Normal Move actions can also set actor speed directly.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Imported [i]quickQuestion[/i] commands open through the normal Question editor.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][i]fade[/i], [i]fade unfade[/i], [i]globalFade[/i] and [i]globalFadeToClear[/i] all use the Fade editor and export back to the appropriate vanilla form.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Imported [i]specificTemporarySprite[/i] commands have their own visual editor. The catalog contains 160 Stardew Valley 1.6.15 routine IDs, and 148 of them have data-only visual simulation recipes for preview.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Unknown commands are stored as Raw actions. Their original command text is preserved instead of being removed during import or export.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[heading][size=5]Questions and branches[/size][/heading]
[size=4]The Question editor supports three workflows: Event Result, Game Key and Quick Question.[/size]

[size=4]A normal Question can connect to a Fork branch. If that branch does not exist yet, Event Studio can create it and open a separate branch timeline with the same Actions and editors used by the main sequence.[/size]

[size=4]Fork follows vanilla behavior: it replaces the rest of the script with the target branch. Quick Question runs the selected answer's action sequence and then returns to the main sequence.[/size]

[size=4]Quick Question uses a fragile vanilla string format. Event Studio rejects nested Quick Questions and ambiguous separator combinations rather than exporting text the game may parse incorrectly.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Dialogue editor[/size][/heading]
[size=4]Dialogue is edited as separate pages instead of one long event command.[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]Multiple pages in one Dialogue action.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Portrait expression selection per page.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Extra portrait frames found in the NPC's portrait sheet.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Multiline text input.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]17 supported vanilla text placeholders.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Placeholders shown as editable tags instead of raw syntax.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Vanilla gender-dependent text through [b]+ Gender text[/b].[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Optional i18n key for exported localization.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[size=4]Normal vanilla dialogue syntax can still be pasted directly. The tags are only an editing aid; the exported event keeps the correct vanilla tokens.[/size]

[size=4]Canvas Preview estimates a reading time for each page so dialogue can participate in timeline playback. That estimate is not written into the exported event. In the game, dialogue still waits for player input as usual.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Preview[/size][/heading]
[size=4][b]Canvas Preview[/b] is the fast editing preview. You can scrub backward and forward through the timeline while Event Studio simulates the scene at the selected point. It handles actor movement and facing, camera changes, routes, dialogue, overhead text, held items, emotes, jumps, shakes, animation, props and supported visual effects.[/size]

[size=4][b]In-game Preview[/b] builds a real Stardew Valley Event and lets the game run the supported parts of the sequence. Event Studio intercepts commands that could leave unwanted changes in the save.[/size]

[size=4]Reward actions use an isolated preview ledger, so you can test money, inventory changes, friendship, quests and mail flags without permanently applying those values. Preview-created props and temporary visuals are tracked separately, the previous music is restored afterward, and the Event is configured not to mark itself as seen.[/size]

[size=4]Questions and Fork branches also pass through the preview system. Named Sprite Effects use Event Studio's data-only renderer instead of running their native story routines just to reproduce the visuals.[/size]

[size=4]If Event Studio cannot safely restore or simulate a command, it skips that command during preview and writes the reason to the SMAPI log.[/size]

[size=4]Because this is a beta build, keep a backup of any save you care about while testing events.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Importing existing events[/size][/heading]
[size=4]Event Studio can read the final event entries loaded from [i]Data/Events/<Location>[/i]. It reads them after Content Patcher has modified the asset, so events added or changed by other content packs can be imported too.[/size]

[size=4]Commands Event Studio understands become structured Actions. Anything else stays editable as Raw command text.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Saving and export[/size][/heading]
[size=4]Projects are stored as versioned [i].svesproject[/i] JSON files in the mod's [i]projects[/i] directory.[/size]

[size=4]You can use normal Save and Save As, timed autosaves, optional autosave on close, recovery entries and [i].bak[/i] backups when an existing project is replaced.[/size]

[size=4]Keep the project file if you want to edit the scene again later. The exported content pack contains the playable event, not the Event Studio project itself.[/size]

[size=4]Export creates:[/size]
[list]
[*][size=4][i]manifest.json[/i][/size][/*]
[*][size=4][i]content.json[/i][/size][/*]
[*][size=4][i]i18n/default.json[/i][/size][/*]
[/list]
[size=4]The project controls its event ID, author, description, version and pack UniqueID. Dialogue Actions with an i18n key are written into the generated localization file automatically.[/size]

[size=4]Fork branches can also be exported as separate event entries, including branches that target another location.[/size]

[size=4]Generated packs are written to the mod's [i]exports[/i] directory. Test the exported pack normally before publishing it, since the final Content Patcher event is what players will actually run.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Interface language and font support[/size][/heading]
[size=4][b]The beta ships with an English interface translation.[/b][/size]

[size=4]Event Studio uses SMAPI i18n, so more interface translations can be added through [i]i18n/<locale>.json[/i]. Changing Stardew Valley's language will only change Event Studio if a matching translation file exists.[/size]

[size=4]The editor does not use a system font. Its text comes from bundled Noto Sans Regular and Bold texture atlases, so the glyphs in those atlases determine which scripts the UI can display.[/size]

[size=4]The bundled atlas contains Basic Latin, Latin-1 Supplement, Latin Extended-A and Extended-B characters, Cyrillic and extended Cyrillic characters, plus common punctuation.[/size]

[size=4]This covers English and most European languages written with the Latin alphabet, including Polish, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Czech, Slovak, Romanian, Hungarian and Turkish. It also covers Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian, Bulgarian, Macedonian and Serbian Cyrillic, plus additional Cyrillic characters used by several other languages.[/size]

[size=4]Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Greek, Arabic, Hebrew, Thai and other scripts outside the bundled atlas are not supported yet. Complex-script shaping is not implemented either. Unsupported characters appear as [i]?[/i].[/size]

[size=4]Russian and Polish translations can therefore use the bundled fonts as-is. Japanese would need additional glyphs and font work first.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Settings[/size][/heading]
[size=4]Open Settings from the toolbar or press [b]Ctrl+,[/b].[/size]

[size=4]Available themes are Dark, Light, Midnight and Parchment. You can choose one of six accent presets or enter a custom [i]#RRGGBB[/i] color.[/size]

[size=4]Workflow settings cover the default grid and collision overlay, timed autosaving, autosave on close, autosave interval and whether Event Studio should reopen automatically after an in-game preview.[/size]

[size=4]Theme changes are previewed immediately. Apply saves them to [i]config.json[/i]. Cancel or Escape restores the previously saved appearance.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Limitations[/size][/heading]
[list]
[*][size=4]Visual editors do not cover every vanilla event command yet. Unsupported commands can be kept as Raw actions.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]The editor is intended for single-player.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Canvas Preview is a simulation for editing. Stardew Valley's own Event runtime remains the reference for exact game behavior.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Reward preview tracks the values Event Studio needs, but it does not simulate every possible downstream inventory, relationship or quest side effect.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Map previews reproduce the important static layers, but they may differ from the game when another mod adds custom rendering, unusual map effects, lighting or animation.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Sound discovery depends on what Stardew Valley exposes through its sound-bank API. You can enter exact cue IDs manually.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Compatibility has not been tested with every custom NPC, map, event framework or heavily modified game setup.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]The bundled UI font covers Latin and Cyrillic text, not every writing system.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[heading][size=5]Feedback and bug reports[/size][/heading]
[size=4]For bug reports, please include enough information to reproduce the problem:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]Your SMAPI log.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Stardew Valley and SMAPI versions.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]What you were trying to build.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]What happened instead.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]The relevant [i].svesproject[/i] file if you can share it.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]A screenshot for interface problems.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Resolution, game zoom and UI scale for layout issues.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Other mods that modify events, maps, NPCs, rendering or audio if the issue looks compatibility-related.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[size=4]Feedback does not have to be a bug report. I'm also interested in what you tried to make, what saved you time, where the workflow felt awkward, and anything you expected the editor to handle differently.[/size]
